newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities end nervous bourse session lower.
newsitem.headline: German equities end nervous bourse session lower.

text.p: German shares end bourse trade slightly lower on Wednesday as the market reacted nervously to the overnight weakness of the U.S. Dow Jones index, despite the support of a strong dollar against the mark.
The DAX index of Germany's 30 leading blue-chips closed trade 4.15 points, or 0.16 percent, down at 2,566.80 points, practically unchanged from opening levels.
Dealers said there were renewed concerns about an early U.S. interest rate increase.

While the strength of the dollar provided support, dealers said the mood of uncertainty would intensify from Thursday ahead of a raft of U.S. data due on Thursday and Friday which could be taken as a possible influence on U.S. interest rates.

"We've only got the Beige Book (on the U.S. economy at 1600 GMT) today which isn't expected to yield much but concern will start making itself felt more from tomorrow," one said, noting the publication of U.S. August producer prices on Thursday.
The latest U.S. money supply data is also due late Thursday, with August consumer prices and retail sales figures in the U.S. due Friday.
Export-led stocks such as those in the chemical sector showed gains because of the higher dollar.
Hoechst AG, which ended up 20 pfennigs at 53.20 marks, and Bayer AG, which closed up 44 pfennigs at 54.37, were among the strongest DAX-30 shares.
Deutsche Bank AG continued to suffer from the problems at its London-based Morgan Grenfell asset management unit, with its shares ending at 71.25 marks, 25 pfennigs down on the day.
